many mods and users are aware of the problems caused by spam, malicious trolls, vote brigading, etc.

up to this point the consensus seems to be to let the community handle the problems by way of down-voting and commenting, however i propose that there may be an additional and potentially more effective solution that essentially enhances this premise by leveraging user blacklists

any sub moderator would than have the choice of a) whether to subscribe to a blacklist and b) what lists to subscribe to - by allowing the mods to make the decision, the blacklists are not forced on anyone and potential censorship problems are minimized

in more detail, i think the blacklists should be granular in that there could be many, each addressing a very specific issues

user names could be published to dedicated subs, but i would think that publishing them to a specially designed area for this purpose would be more efficient

moderators then have a check-boxed list of blacklists they want to subscribe to and upon subscribing to a list, all of the users in it are auto-banned from that particular sub

user names are added to blacklists by moderators/maintainers of the lists after a review of the submission (is there a legit reason for adding this user?)

submissions are made by moderators only, at least in the early stage of implementation

another way to implement this would be to allow users (and *not* mods) to subscribe to the lists, since i think blocking individual users (not implemented at this time) is simply not efficient or effective in all cases
possible method to combat spam, trolls, etc., using dedicated subs and a blacklist - your thoughts?
